sources.locator: "Paris Peace Accords", revision 1376485436, § Breakthrough and agreement

explanation: The Accords article makes the offensive's result one of the things that moved Hanoi at the table: "The final major breakthrough came on October 8, 1972. Prior to this, North Vietnam had been disappointed by the results of its Nguyen Hue Offensive (known in the West as the Easter Offensive), which had resulted in the United States countering with 'Operation Linebacker', a significant air bombing campaign that blunted the North's drive in the South as well as inflicting damage in the North." In the same paragraph Thọ "significantly modified his bargaining line, allowing that the Saigon government could remain in power", and within ten days the secret talks drew up a final draft. The Easter Offensive article reaches the same point from its own side: "In Paris, the peace negotiations continued, but this time, both sides were willing to make concessions." Enabled and not caused: the article names the offensive's disappointing result as one of the conditions of the breakthrough, beside Hanoi's fear of isolation as Nixon's détente improved relations with Moscow and Beijing, and does not make it the cause of the agreement. Probable: Wikipedia alone (rule 22).
